Monetary policy surprise factors from a panel of financial market series

Source: R/gss_pca.R
gss_pca.Rd

Estimates one or two factors from a panel of event-window changes of financial market series (rows are events, columns are series), following Gurkaynak, Sack and Swanson (2005):

  • n_factors = 1: a single common factor ("overall" surprise), the first principal component of the standardised panel.

  • n_factors = 2: two factors rotated such that the second factor ("path") has a zero loading on the first column of X. The first factor ("target") is then the only factor that moves the first series.

Usage

gss_pca(
  X,
  n_factors = 2,
  norm_anchor = seq_len(n_factors),
  tol = 1e-08,
  maxit = 500
)

# S3 method for class 'gss_pca'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

X

Numeric matrix or data frame (T x N) of event-window changes, with only the financial market series as columns. For n_factors = 2, the first column defines the target restriction (the path factor has a zero loading on it).

n_factors

Integer. 1 (overall factor) or 2 (target and path factors, default).

norm_anchor

Integer vector of length n_factors with the column positions in X against which the factors are normalised. Defaults to 1 or c(1, 2). For n_factors = 2, norm_anchor[2] cannot be 1.

tol

Numeric. Convergence tolerance of the EM iterations.

maxit

Integer. Maximum number of EM iterations.

x

An object of class gss_pca.

...

Ignored.

Value

A list of class gss_pca with elements:

factors

Matrix T x n_factors with columns "overall" or "target" and "path", in the units of the anchor series.

loadings

Matrix N x n_factors of loadings of the standardised series on the (rotated and normalised) factors.

var_explained

Share of the variance of the standardised panel explained by each unrotated principal component.

restriction

For n_factors = 2: loading of the path factor on the first series (zero up to numerical error); NULL otherwise.

norm_anchor

Named character vector with the anchor series of each factor.

norm_coef

Named vector with the regression coefficient to which each factor was calibrated.

mu, sd

Means and standard deviations of the series used for standardisation.

X_filled

Standardised panel with missing cells replaced by their EM fit.

n_missing, iters, converged, call

Number of missing cells, number of EM iterations, convergence flag, and the call.

Details

Missing values are handled by EM principal components (Stock and Watson, 2002; Swanson, 2021): missing cells are initialised at the mean and iteratively replaced by their fit from the n_factors principal components until convergence.

The factors are normalised against series in X through regression coefficients, as in Gurkaynak, Sack and Swanson (2005):

  • n_factors = 1: the factor is rescaled such that the coefficient of a regression of X[, norm_anchor[1]] on the factor is one (a one-unit move of the factor is a one-unit move of its anchor series).

  • n_factors = 2: the target factor is rescaled in the same way against X[, norm_anchor[1]]. The path factor is rescaled such that its coefficient on X[, norm_anchor[2]] equals the coefficient of the target factor on the same series.

The anchor regressions use the rows where the anchor series is observed.

References

Gurkaynak, R. S., Sack, B. and Swanson, E. T. (2005). Do actions speak louder than words? The response of asset prices to monetary policy actions and statements. International Journal of Central Banking, 1(1), 55-93.

Stock, J. H. and Watson, M. W. (2002). Macroeconomic forecasting using diffusion indexes. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 20(2), 147-162.

Swanson, E. T. (2021). Measuring the effects of Federal Reserve forward guidance and asset purchases on financial markets. Journal of Monetary Economics, 118, 32-53.

Examples

# Simulated panel: 5 series driven by a target and a path factor; the first
# series responds to the target factor only
set.seed(1)
f <- matrix(rnorm(400), ncol = 2)
L <- cbind(c(1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2), c(0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.8, 1))
X <- f %*% t(L) + matrix(rnorm(1000, sd = 0.1), ncol = 5)
colnames(X) <- paste0("r", 1:5)
X[3, 4] <- NA
res <- gss_pca(X, n_factors = 2)
res
#> gss_pca: 2 factor(s) [target, path], 200 events x 5 series, 1 missing cells
#> var explained (PC1..PC2): 76.5%, 22.7%
#> path loading on 'r1' (target restriction, should be 0): 2.75e-16
#> normalisation: target -> coef 1.000 on 'r1'; path -> coef 0.794 on 'r2'
#> loadings:
#>    target  path
#> r1  1.061 0.000
#> r2  0.980 0.980
#> r3  0.701 1.932
#> r4  0.411 2.381
#> r5  0.165 2.556
head(res$factors)
#>          target        path
#> [1,] -0.6042134  0.09805403
#> [2,]  0.2541628  0.63802917
#> [3,] -0.8198619  0.54913400
#> [4,]  1.6079106 -0.15266963
#> [5,]  0.2529482 -0.86567612
#> [6,] -0.9417266  0.91834664
